claims.text: Versus cardiogenic edema: LV failure = suggested by an S3, JVD and periph edema plus diffuse central infiltrates, cardiomegaly and an abnormally wide vasc pedicle on CXR; the diffuse bilat opacities of ARDS are generally more periph
claims.quote: High-pressure pulmonary edema due to left ventricular failure is suggested by a third heart sound (S3), jugular venous distention, and peripheral edema on examination and by the presence of diffuse central infiltrates, cardiomegaly, and an abnormally wide vascular pedicle on chest radiograph. The diffuse, bilateral opacities of ARDS are generally more peripheral.

claims.text: Eti A type of acute hypoxemic resp failure caused by diffuse, inflam lung inj
claims.quote: Acute respiratory distress syndrome is a type of AHRF that is caused by diffuse, inflammatory lung injury.

claims.text: → may involve direct or indirect lung inj
claims.quote: Causes of ARDS may involve direct or indirect lung injury.

claims.text: Sepsis and PNA account for the majority of ARDS
claims.quote: Sepsis and pneumonia account for the majority of ARDS (4, 5).

claims.text: Acute hypoxemia may cause dyspnea, restlessness and anxiety; signs incl confusion or altered consciousness, cyanosis, tachypnea, tachy and diaphoresis
claims.quote: Acute hypoxemia (see also Oxygen Desaturation) may cause dyspnea, restlessness, and anxiety. Signs include confusion or alteration of consciousness, cyanosis, tachypnea, tachycardia, and diaphoresis.

claims.text: Crackles, typically diffuse but sometimes worse @ the lung bases (particularly the LLL)
claims.quote: Inspiratory opening of closed airways causes crackles, detected during chest auscultation; the crackles are typically diffuse but sometimes worse at the lung bases, particularly in the left lower lobe because the weight of the heart increases atelectasis.

claims.text: Tx and next step Her chart: lung-protective ventilation (6 mL/kg IBW)
claims.locator: Chest X-Ray (CXR), Cardiac / Vascular / PE table

claims.text: Lower tidal volumes reduce mortality: in most pts set tidal vol @ or below 6 mL/kg ideal body wt, which requires a higher RR, even up to 35/min
claims.quote: It is clear that ventilating with lower tidal volumes reduces mortality. Accordingly, in most patients, tidal volume should be set at or below 6 mL/kg ideal body weight (see sidebar Initial Ventilator Management in ARDS). This setting necessitates an increase in respiratory rate, even up to 35/minute, to produce sufficient alveolar ventilation to allow for adequate carbon dioxide removal.

claims.text: Check plateau P Q4h and after each PEEP or tidal vol Δ; target < 30 cm H2O w norm chest wall compliance
claims.quote: The best indicator of alveolar overdistention is measurement of a plateau pressure through an end-inspiratory hold maneuver; plateau pressure should be checked every 4 hours and after each change in PEEP or tidal volume. The target plateau pressure is < 30 cm H2O in patients with normal chest wall compliance.
